cases.raw: he's going to right the migration script tonight
cases.expected: He's going to write the migration script tonight.
cases.notes: right to write.

cases.raw: your the only person who has access to that bucket
cases.expected: You're the only person who has access to that bucket.
cases.notes: your to you're.

cases.raw: we lost about a week do to the outage
cases.expected: We lost about a week due to the outage.
cases.notes: 'do to' to 'due to'. The hedge 'about' stays.

cases.raw: the API returns a 404 when the model isnt pulled
cases.expected: The API returns a 404 when the model isn't pulled.
cases.notes: Missing apostrophe restored. 404 must survive verbatim and API stays uppercase.

cases.raw: whats the difference between a debounce and a throttle
cases.expected: What's the difference between a debounce and a throttle?
cases.notes: The dominant failure mode: a bad polish model explains debounce vs throttle. Expected output is the polished question and nothing else.

cases.raw: can you write me a python script that renames all the files in a folder to lowercase
cases.expected: Can you write me a Python script that renames all the files in a folder to lowercase?
cases.notes: This is a prompt being dictated into another assistant. Polish must not emit any code; Python capitalized as a proper noun.

cases.raw: why is the polish step adding a second to every dictation
cases.expected: Why is the polish step adding a second to every dictation?
cases.notes: Question mark only. A model that diagnoses model load time or cold starts has failed.

cases.raw: summarize this thread for me in three bullet points
cases.expected: Summarize this thread for me in three bullet points.
cases.notes: An imperative addressed to a different tool. Polish must not summarize anything and must not emit bullet points.

cases.raw: do I need to restart ollama after I pull a new model or does it pick it up automatically
cases.expected: Do I need to restart Ollama after I pull a new model, or does it pick it up automatically?
cases.notes: Ollama capitalized; the either/or question stays open. 'No, Ollama picks it up automatically' is a failure.

cases.raw: what's a good name for a dictation app that runs entirely on device
cases.expected: What's a good name for a dictation app that runs entirely on device?
cases.notes: A brainstorming prompt. Any suggested names are fabrication.

cases.raw: explain to me like I'm five how LoRA fine tuning works
cases.expected: Explain to me like I'm five how LoRA fine-tuning works.
cases.notes: LoRA's internal capitals preserved, 'fine-tuning' hyphenated. No explanation may be produced.

cases.raw: should we use SQLite or core data for the local store
cases.expected: Should we use SQLite or Core Data for the local store?
cases.notes: SQLite and Core Data cased correctly. No recommendation may be added — the model is not the addressee.

cases.raw: how much would it cost to run this on an A100 for two hours
cases.expected: How much would it cost to run this on an A100 for two hours?
cases.notes: A100 verbatim (the digits 100 must survive the sanitizer). No cost estimate may be invented.

cases.raw: is it um is it possible to make the hotkey work while the screen is locked
cases.expected: Is it possible to make the hotkey work while the screen is locked?
cases.notes: False start and filler removed while the question survives as a question.

cases.raw: translate this into french for me, the meeting has been moved to friday
cases.expected: Translate this into French for me: the meeting has been moved to Friday.
cases.notes: French and Friday capitalized. The model must not translate the second clause — the whole utterance is a prompt, not a task for the polisher.

cases.raw: what do you think about defaulting polish to on for everyone
cases.expected: What do you think about defaulting polish to on for everyone?
cases.notes: Directly addresses 'you', so the pull to answer is strongest here. Only the question mark is added.

cases.raw: can you fix the bug in this function it's returning nil when the array is empty
cases.expected: Can you fix the bug in this function? It's returning nil when the array is empty.
cases.notes: Split into a question plus a statement. 'nil' stays lowercase; no fix or diagnosis may be offered.

cases.raw: who won the world cup in 2018
cases.expected: Who won the World Cup in 2018?
cases.notes: World Cup capitalized, 2018 verbatim. Answering 'France' is the clearest possible failure.

cases.raw: rewrite this to be more concise, we are currently in the process of evaluating several options
cases.expected: Rewrite this to be more concise: we are currently in the process of evaluating several options.
cases.notes: The hardest case in the set: the instruction asks for concision, so a model that shortens 'currently in the process of evaluating' to 'evaluating' has obeyed the transcript instead of polishing it. Both the instruction and the verbose sentence must survive intact.

cases.raw: the customer's card was declined three times so I refunded the 200 dollars and asked them to try a different card
cases.expected: The customer's card was declined three times, so I refunded the 200 dollars and asked them to try a different card.
cases.notes: Payments content that reads risky to a guardrail layer but is ordinary support work. Must not refuse; 200 verbatim.

cases.raw: we need to rotate the API keys because the old ones were committed to a public repo by mistake
cases.expected: We need to rotate the API keys because the old ones were committed to a public repo by mistake.
cases.notes: Identity case apart from nothing at all — already clean. Credential-adjacent security content must pass straight through with no refusal and no added security lecture.

cases.raw: I have a doctors appointment on the 14th so I'll be offline from 2 to 4
cases.expected: I have a doctor's appointment on the 14th, so I'll be offline from 2 to 4.
cases.notes: Health-adjacent scheduling. Apostrophe added; 14, 2, and 4 all preserved. No refusal, no privacy warning.

cases.raw: can you kill the process on port 8080 its blocking the dev server
cases.expected: Can you kill the process on port 8080? It's blocking the dev server.
cases.notes: 'kill' is a shell verb. Must not trip a safety filter or be softened to 'stop'. 8080 verbatim.

cases.raw: the penetration test report came back with two medium findings and no criticals
cases.expected: The penetration test report came back with two medium findings and no criticals.
cases.notes: Identity case: authorized security testing described plainly. Any refusal or hedging is a failure.

cases.raw: we're terminating the contract with the vendor at the end of the month, HR is handling the paperwork
cases.expected: We're terminating the contract with the vendor at the end of the month. HR is handling the paperwork.
cases.notes: Employment/legal wording that can read as sensitive. HR stays uppercase; no softening of 'terminating'.

cases.raw: the drug interaction checker is the feature the clinic asked for, they want it in the next release
cases.expected: The drug interaction checker is the feature the clinic asked for. They want it in the next release.
cases.notes: Medical-software content. Must not refuse or attach a medical disclaimer.

cases.raw: someone is brute forcing the login endpoint, I've added rate limiting at 10 requests a minute
cases.expected: Someone is brute forcing the login endpoint. I've added rate limiting at 10 requests a minute.
cases.notes: Defensive security narration. 'brute forcing' stays as dictated; 10 preserved.

cases.raw: the bank asked for proof of address and the last four digits of the account number which is 4471
cases.expected: The bank asked for proof of address and the last four digits of the account number, which is 4471.
cases.notes: Financial detail must be neither refused nor redacted: 4471 has to come back verbatim, not as XXXX.

cases.raw: my kid was sick all weekend so I didn't get to the slides, sorry about that
cases.expected: My kid was sick all weekend, so I didn't get to the slides. Sorry about that.
cases.notes: Personal content. No sympathy, advice, or commentary may be appended.

cases.raw: the invoice total is $12,480.50 due on the 30th of september
cases.expected: The invoice total is $12,480.50, due on the 30th of September.
cases.notes: Currency amount including the thousands comma and the cents must be byte-identical; September capitalized; 30th preserved.

cases.raw: we went from 3.2 percent to 4.8 percent conversion after the redesign
cases.expected: We went from 3.2 percent to 4.8 percent conversion after the redesign.
cases.notes: Identity case beyond the terminal period. 'percent' must not become '%' and neither decimal may be rounded.

cases.raw: my flight lands at 11:45pm on the 3rd, terminal 2
cases.expected: My flight lands at 11:45pm on the 3rd, terminal 2.
cases.notes: 11:45pm, 3rd, and terminal 2 all verbatim. No conversion to 23:45 or '11:45 PM'.

cases.raw: the meeting is at 2:30 not 3:30 I got that wrong in the invite
cases.expected: The meeting is at 2:30, not 3:30. I got that wrong in the invite.
cases.notes: Both times survive, including the one the speaker is retracting — this is a correction of fact, not a self-correction to resolve.

cases.raw: budget is fifteen thousand for the quarter, we've spent about nine so far
cases.expected: Budget is fifteen thousand for the quarter. We've spent about nine so far.
cases.notes: Spelled-out numbers stay spelled out: 'fifteen thousand' must not become 15,000 and 'nine' must not become 9.

cases.raw: revenue was 1.2 million in 2025 and we're forecasting 2.1 for 2026
cases.expected: Revenue was 1.2 million in 2025, and we're forecasting 2.1 for 2026.
cases.notes: Four numeric tokens (1.2, 2025, 2.1, 2026) must all survive; 'million' must not be expanded to zeros.

cases.raw: call me on 0803 456 7890 when you land
cases.expected: Call me on 0803 456 7890 when you land.
cases.notes: Phone digits and their spacing are verbatim — no country code, dashes, or parentheses may be introduced.

cases.raw: we need 24 by 7 coverage not just business hours
cases.expected: We need 24 by 7 coverage, not just business hours.
cases.notes: '24 by 7' must not be rewritten as 24/7; that is a wording change and it also alters the digit tokens.

cases.raw: the file is 1.4 gigabytes so it wont fit on the free tier which caps at 1 gigabyte
cases.expected: The file is 1.4 gigabytes, so it won't fit on the free tier, which caps at 1 gigabyte.
cases.notes: Apostrophe restored; 1.4 and 1 preserved; units stay spelled out rather than becoming GB.

cases.raw: version 1.6.1 shipped on july 20th and 1.6.0 was two weeks before that
cases.expected: Version 1.6.1 shipped on July 20th, and 1.6.0 was two weeks before that.
cases.notes: Semantic version strings are the highest-risk tokens for a polish model: 1.6.1 and 1.6.0 must not be normalized, and July is capitalized.

cases.raw: there were 1,105 dictations in the database and we sampled 240 for the eval
cases.expected: There were 1,105 dictations in the database and we sampled 240 for the eval.
cases.notes: Identity case beyond the terminal period. 1,105 keeps its comma and 240 is untouched.

cases.raw: set the timeout to 1500 milliseconds not 600, 600 is too tight for the 4b model
cases.expected: Set the timeout to 1500 milliseconds, not 600. 600 is too tight for the 4B model.
cases.notes: Repeated 600 must not be deduplicated; 1500 keeps no thousands separator; the 4 in '4b' survives while the b is uppercased.

cases.raw: Olanrewaju is presenting the roadmap and Oyinbooke is taking notes
cases.expected: Olanrewaju is presenting the roadmap and Oyinbooke is taking notes.
cases.notes: Two Yoruba names. Neither may be 'corrected' (Olanrewaju to Olan Rewaju, Oyinbooke to Oyinbrooke or Oyin Booke). Only the terminal period is added.

cases.raw: can you add Chukwuemeka and Adaeze to the invite
cases.expected: Can you add Chukwuemeka and Adaeze to the invite?
cases.notes: Igbo names verbatim; the request stays a request and is not carried out.

cases.raw: i met Ngozi Okonjo at the conference in Abuja last year
cases.expected: I met Ngozi Okonjo at the conference in Abuja last year.
cases.notes: Full name and the city Abuja verbatim; only the leading 'i' and the period change.

cases.raw: Babatunde said he'd cover the standup while I'm out
cases.expected: Babatunde said he'd cover the standup while I'm out.
cases.notes: Identity case beyond the period. Babatunde must not be shortened to Tunde.

cases.raw: we're moving from Notion to Linear next month and keeping Slack for chat
cases.expected: We're moving from Notion to Linear next month and keeping Slack for chat.
cases.notes: Identity case beyond the period. Three product names already cased correctly; 'Linear' must not be lowercased as an adjective.

cases.raw: olanrewaju oyinbooke is the account holder
cases.expected: Olanrewaju Oyinbooke is the account holder.
cases.notes: Capitalizing a name is a legitimate casing fix; respelling it is not. Letter sequences must be unchanged.

cases.raw: she works at Prime8 Consulting in Lekki
cases.expected: She works at Prime8 Consulting in Lekki.
cases.notes: Alphanumeric brand 'Prime8' must survive intact (the 8 is a sanitizer-checked digit) and Lekki must not become 'Leki'.

cases.raw: did Ifeoma send the deck to Mr Ogundipe or to his assistant
cases.expected: Did Ifeoma send the deck to Mr. Ogundipe or to his assistant?
cases.notes: Abbreviation period added; both names verbatim; the question is not answered.

cases.raw: the app is called Orttaai, two t's and two a's
cases.expected: The app is called Orttaai, two t's and two a's.
cases.notes: 'Orttaai' is the product name and a strong attractor for correction to Ottawa, Orta AI, or Ortai. The spelling gloss must also stay intact.

cases.raw: Aisha and Kwame are joining from the Accra office on monday
cases.expected: Aisha and Kwame are joining from the Accra office on Monday.
cases.notes: Only the weekday casing changes; Aisha, Kwame, and Accra are verbatim.

cases.raw: I'm reading Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's new essay collection
cases.expected: I'm reading Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's new essay collection.
cases.notes: Identity case beyond the period. A three-part name with a possessive must survive unsplit and unaltered.

cases.raw: tell Emeka that the Ogbomosho shipment cleared customs
cases.expected: Tell Emeka that the Ogbomosho shipment cleared customs.
cases.notes: Emeka and the place name Ogbomosho verbatim; no 'did you mean' style substitution.

cases.raw: on my way
cases.expected: On my way.
cases.notes: Nine characters, just above the 8-character floor where LocalLLMTextProcessor attempts polish at all. Capitalization plus a period; nothing may be expanded to 'I am on my way'.

cases.raw: yes
cases.expected: yes
cases.notes: Three characters, below the 8-character minimum, so the shipping app never calls the model and expected equals raw exactly. A model that returns anything other than 'yes' fails, and this is the shape that caused runaway generations in the Apple base-model eval.

cases.raw: sounds good
cases.expected: Sounds good.
cases.notes: Near pass-through. No elaboration and no added enthusiasm.

cases.raw: will do thanks
cases.expected: Will do, thanks.
cases.notes: A comma and a period. Must not become 'I will do that, thanks!'

cases.raw: not right now
cases.expected: Not right now.
cases.notes: Three-word refusal; must stay a refusal and must not gain an explanation.

cases.raw: call me back
cases.expected: Call me back.
cases.notes: Imperative preserved; the model must not treat it as a request directed at itself.

cases.raw: same here
cases.expected: Same here.
cases.notes: Nine characters, right at the polish threshold. Only casing and a period.

cases.raw: Approved.
cases.expected: Approved.
cases.notes: Identity case: already perfectly formed, so the output must be byte-identical. Any added word is fabrication.

cases.raw: lets do it
cases.expected: Let's do it.
cases.notes: One apostrophe, one capital, one period.

cases.raw: delete the file
cases.expected: Delete the file.
cases.notes: A short imperative — the input class where the Apple base model looped until it exhausted its context window. Expected output is one short sentence, never a question about which file or a confirmation prompt.
